newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian diamond group to open 3 overseas offices.
newsitem.headline: Russian diamond group to open 3 overseas offices.

text.p: Russia's Almazy Rossii-Sakha diamond producer, partner to De Beers in a still-unsigned gem export agreement, said on Thursday that it would open three representative offices in key international diamond centres.

But Andrei Kirillin, chairman of ARS's supervisory council, a body which fulfills some of the functions of the board, said no changes had been made to the draft text of a stalled diamond export agreement now undergoing Russian government scrutiny.
Kirillin said three offices -- in London, Antwerp and Luanda, Angola -- would work to gather information on world diamond markets.
"We will open these three offices because we are interested in having more information," he said. "De Beers has 60 offices -- why shouldn't we have some?"
When asked when a long-delayed trade deal with the South African gem giant could be signed, he said, "Maybe in February.
"This is what we are hoping for, but it does not depend upon us -- rather, it depends upon the government," he said.
When asked if the text of the draft trade agreement the government was considering had been changed, he said, "No," adding, "any right-thinking person wants a deal with De Beers".
ARS President Vyacheslav Shtyrov said last Saturday that Russia could approve a deal this month, but a De Beers official in Moscow cast doubt upon the time-frame.
De Beers stopped all purchases of diamonds from Russia on December 31 when it cancelled an interim arrangement after the Russian authorities failed to approve or reject the draft of a new trade deal.

Some senior Russian government officials said in December 1996 that the draft needed reworking. They later said Russia needed an export deal with De Beers, but have thus far failed to resolve the impasse.
De Beers controls about three quarters of the world diamond market and according to the proposed trade agreement Russia would deliver to De Beers 26 per cent of the South African company's sales.
